events.title: Establishment of Vinh Binh Province (Predecessor of Tra Vinh)
events.description: During the administrative reform of King Minh Mang, the Six Provinces of Southern Vietnam were divided into new provinces. Vinh Binh Province was established (including present-day Tra Vinh territory), as an important province located between the two major rivers, Tien and Hau.

events.title: Establishment of the First Party Cell (An Truong)
events.description: In An Truong Village, the first Communist Party Cell of Tra Vinh Province was established, with Comrade Nguyen Dang (alias Bay Dang) as Secretary. This event marked an important turning point, bringing the struggle movement of the people of Tra Vinh into the orbit of the proletarian revolution.

events.title: Seizing Power in Tra Vinh
events.description: More than 20,000 people from Cang Long, Chau Thanh, and Cau Ngang Districts flocked to the provincial capital. Faced with overwhelming momentum, the Governor of Tra Vinh Province had to surrender and hand over the official seal. The Provisional Administrative Committee of Tra Vinh Province made its debut to the public.

events.title: La Bang Victory
events.description: Battalion 307 and local armed forces organized an ambush on a French military convoy at La Bang. We destroyed many motor vehicles and enemy soldiers. This was a typical road-battle, making the name of 'Battalion 307' famous across the Southwestern region battlefield.

events.title: Cau Ke Campaign
events.description: The Command of Zone 8 launched the Cau Ke Campaign; this was the first large-scale offensive campaign in the Southern battlefield with coordination between regular and local forces, destroying many outposts and expanding the liberated area.

events.title: The Legend of 'The Mother with a Gun' Nguyen Thi Ut
events.description: Mrs. Nguyen Thi Ut (Ut Tich), a daughter of the Tam Ngai land, was famous for her saying 'Fight even if only the hem of the pants is left'. She participated in dozens of battles, serving as a symbol of the heroic and indomitable Southern women during the resistance war against the US.

events.title: Tet Mau Than in Tra Vinh
events.description: The army and people of Tra Vinh simultaneously attacked the Governor's Palace, the Police Department, and the enemy's headquarters in the town. We controlled the central area of the town for many hours, causing extreme panic for the local Saigon government apparatus.

events.title: Building Uncle Ho's Temple (Long Duc)
events.description: Right in the midst of the enemy's fierce siege, the army and people of Long Duc Commune secretly built Uncle Ho's Temple to express their infinite love upon hearing the news of his passing. The temple was resiliently protected through 5 years of bombs and bullets (1970-1975) until the day of complete victory.

events.title: Liberation of Tra Vinh Province
events.description: The provincial armed forces coordinated with the masses to surround and attack the Governor's Palace. At exactly 11:30 AM on April 30, 1975, the Front's flag flew on top of the Governor's Palace; Tra Vinh was completely liberated, without much bloodshed as the enemy surrendered quickly.

events.title: Re-establishment of Tra Vinh Province
events.description: The 8th National Assembly passed a Resolution to split Cuu Long Province (merged since 1976) back into two provinces, Vinh Long and Tra Vinh. Tra Vinh Province officially came into operation, starting the reconstruction and economic development of the coastal region.

events.title: Inauguration of Co Chien Bridge
events.description: Co Chien Bridge, connecting Ben Tre and Tra Vinh, was inaugurated. This project is of strategic significance, breaking the 'dead-end' traffic situation of Tra Vinh, shortening the distance to Ho Chi Minh City, and creating momentum for the development of the marine economy and clean energy.
